environment-1.title: Ecology: relationships, flows and diversity

sections.heading: An ecosystem is a set of interactions
sections.text: Organisms interact with one another and with physical conditions. Producers, consumers and decomposers describe functional roles, not a rigid ranking of importance. Food webs are more realistic than isolated chains because many organisms use several resources. Removing one component can have indirect effects, but their scale depends on the network and local conditions.

sections.heading: Energy and matter behave differently
sections.text: Energy enters many ecosystems through photosynthesis and is dissipated through successive transfers; nutrients can cycle among living organisms, soil, water and the atmosphere. Do not say that energy is recycled in the same way as matter. Ecological pyramids depend on what is being measured, while simple rules of thumb should not be treated as identical observations for every ecosystem.

sections.heading: Diversity has several dimensions
sections.text: Genetic, species and ecosystem diversity describe different levels. Richness counts species, while the balance of their abundance also affects diversity. An endemic species has a restricted geographic distribution; that does not automatically mean it is threatened. Assess habitat, pressures and population evidence separately. This distinction is useful when reading conservation claims and species-based questions.

terms.meaning: The environment in which an organism lives.
An organism’s ecological role and relationships.

timeline.event: Consider direct and indirect effects of change.

environment-1.trap: Endemic, invasive and endangered describe different properties.

practice.question: Why might the loss of one species affect organisms that do not feed directly on it?
practice.answer: Food webs include indirect relationships through predators, competitors, resources and habitat modification. Explain a chain of effects and acknowledge that real systems can respond differently.

mcq: Which is generally recycled through an ecosystem?
Energy in exactly the same form
Nutrients such as carbon and nitrogen
Matter cycles among reservoirs, while usable energy is progressively dissipated.

environment-2.title: Pollution and climate: sources, pathways and impacts

sections.heading: Trace the exposure pathway
sections.text: A pollutant matters through its source, transport, transformation and contact with living systems. Concentration, duration and vulnerability affect harm. A clear river is not necessarily free of dissolved contamination, and dilution does not remove the total pollutant load. Compare prevention at source with treatment after release rather than treating all waste management as an end-of-pipe problem.

sections.heading: Distinguish related atmospheric issues
sections.text: The greenhouse effect concerns the balance of incoming and outgoing energy. Ozone depletion involves a different atmospheric process, although some chemicals connect the issues. Climate is evaluated through longer-term patterns and multiple observations, not a single hot or cold day. Mitigation addresses the drivers of change; adaptation reduces harm from experienced or expected effects.

sections.heading: Choose responses at the right scale
sections.text: Household action, municipal services, industrial regulation and international cooperation act at different levels. A response can shift pollution elsewhere if its full life cycle is ignored. Evaluate trade-offs, monitoring and implementation. For Bihar, water quality, waste handling, flood exposure and agricultural practices connect ecological conditions with health and livelihoods; avoid blaming outcomes on individual behaviour alone.

rows: Dilution can lower one without removing the other.
Do not use the terms interchangeably.

terms.meaning: Contact with a hazard through a pathway.
Nutrient enrichment that can alter aquatic systems.
Stages from resource extraction through use and disposal.

environment-2.trap: A lower concentration after dilution does not mean that the pollutant has ceased to exist.

practice.question: Why should urban air-pollution policy consider more than private cars?
practice.answer: Industry, power, construction, dust, waste burning and other sources can contribute differently by location and season. Use source evidence to prioritise measures and assess exposure, enforcement and alternatives.

mcq: Which is primarily an adaptation measure?
Heat preparedness reduces harm from climatic conditions; the other examples primarily reduce drivers.

environment-3.title: Conservation: ecological outcomes and public institutions

sections.heading: Protection involves people and places
sections.text: A protected boundary is only one part of conservation. Connectivity, habitat quality, enforcement, livelihoods and the rights of affected communities influence results. A conservation category does not by itself reveal management quality. Examine ecological objectives and the institutional arrangements required to achieve them, and use official current sources for legal designations and changing status.

sections.heading: Compare conservation strategies
sections.text: In-situ conservation works within natural habitats; ex-situ approaches operate outside them, such as seed banks or managed breeding. They can complement one another but are not interchangeable. Restoring a degraded ecosystem is more complex than planting any trees: species composition, water, soil, local ecology and long-term maintenance matter. A plantation should not automatically be described as equivalent to a natural forest.

sections.heading: Turn commitments into implementation
sections.text: Environmental governance includes standards, assessment, monitoring, incentives and accountability. International commitments and domestic implementation are distinct steps. Evaluate whether institutions have data, capacity and a response when requirements are violated. For an exam answer, connect environmental protection with distributional questions: who benefits, who bears costs and how participation and remedies are organised.

rows: Can preserve material or support recovery.
Area alone does not capture ecological quality.

terms.meaning: Links allowing ecological movement and interaction.
Helping a degraded ecosystem recover relevant functions and characteristics.
Considering serious uncertain risks before harm becomes established.

environment-3.trap: Tree cover, forest quality and biodiversity are related but not identical indicators.

practice.question: Why might a tree-planting target fail to restore an ecosystem?
practice.answer: Inappropriate species, poor survival, altered water use, loss of open habitats or lack of maintenance can undermine the objective. Define the original ecosystem and measure function and diversity, not only saplings planted.

mcq: Which is an ex-situ conservation example?
A seed bank conserves biological material outside the natural habitat.
